title: Upper Respiratory & Middle Ear Barotrauma Protocol
trigger_patterns: Crew reports nasal congestion, Eustachian tube fullness, or severe otalgia upon swallowing
Nasal-ear score exceeds baseline watch threshold (> 2/10)
Mandatory pre-entry or pre-EVA helmet donning checklist with active upper respiratory symptoms

steps.text: Assess bilateral tympanic membrane mobility and Eustachian tube patency using gentle modified Valsalva/Toynbee maneuver; do NOT force auto-inflation against severe pain.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Record nasal congestion and otalgia severity on the 0-10 scale and log whether unilateral or bilateral obstruction is present.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: If suit or helmet donning is required within 4 hours, administer approved nasal decongestant spray/oral agent to prevent tympanic membrane perforation during rapid repressurization.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Review cabin environmental telemetry: verify habitat relative humidity > 40% and check particulate/HEPA recirculation status.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Implement cabin droplet hygiene protocols: sanitize shared sleep quarters, headsets, and microphone wind-screens to prevent transmission to crewmates.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: If re-entry G-transition is imminent, coordinate with Flight Dynamics to slow capsule repressurization rate if operational envelope permits.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure
